docs.title: HIVE
docs.text:
Hydrodynamic Identification and Validation Environment

HIVE is a Python framework for wave energy converter (WEC) hydrodynamic modelling, identification, and model benchmarking.

docs.title: What HIVE does
docs.text:
HIVE provides structured pipelines to:

  • Process CFD simulation data
  • Validate existing physics and data-based models against CFD reference data
  • Identify model parameters and data-driven surrogates from CFD reference data

docs.title: Key features
docs.text:
• BEM-based linear and weakly-nonlinear hydrodynamic model
  • Viscous drag identification
  • PI gain identification for PTO control
  • Multiple and various data-based model (wave-to-force-to-velocity state-space, system identification for nonlinear dynamic (SINDY), neural network)
  • model benchmarking through large metric bank

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• environment surrogate
  • A HydroSphere BEM pickle file (r5.pkl is the project default) placed under source/models/bem/ for validation and/or identification pipeline
  • A reference raw dataset folder for placed under 'data/cfd/' for handle pipeline
  • A reference handled dataset (.csv) for validation and identification pipeline placed under data/handled/
  • A model (.json) for validation and/or identification pipeline placed under source/models/

docs.title: Quick test run
docs.text:
All scripts are run as modules from inside the code/ folder. A minimal test case is provided using r5.pkl as BEM model and out_Case_65_20_120000_-430000_example as raw reference dataset. Run it with: 

# 1 — process CFD data
python -m script.run_handle_data --case example_cases.json

# 2 — validate models
python -m script.run_validate --case example_validate.json

# 3 — identify parameters
python -m script.run_identify --case example_identify.json

Outputs land in data/handled/example_cases/ (handle data), out/validated_case/example_validate/ (validate), or models/example_identify/identification/ for identification results (identify). When repeating the test run again, a user command is required, choose [1] erase and redo all. More information is available in the user manual.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
This documentation is based on mkdocs and is mostly a log for the code author rather than a package documentation for external users.

To update the documentation, mkdocs gh-deploy should be ran in code/doc/

docs.title: Pipeline Overview
docs.text: HIVE is built around three pipelines ran via scripts, run_handle_data, run_validate and run_identify, each driven by a JSON input file and writing outputs to a structured folder.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Script What it does Config location Output location run_handle_data Reads raw CFD time series, applies cut times and optional resampling, computes wave parameters and hydrodynamic quantities, saves one processed dataset per case inputs/handle_case/<name>.json data/handled/<name>/ run_validate Loads processed datasets and a model.json, runs forward simulations via SimRun, computes metrics against the CFD reference, produces scatter plots over the \((H_s, T_e)\) parameter space inputs/validate_case/<name>.json out/validated_case/<name>/ run_identify Uses a scheme module (viscous_drag, pi_gain, or linear_si) to identify model parameters from CFD data, updates model.json with the result inputs/identify_case/<name>.json models/<name>/ + models/<name>/identification/

Each script read the input .json file --case <name>.json argument. The stem of that filename becomes the output folder name — choose stems that are short, lowercase, and use underscores (e.g. r5_reg).

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Every plot is saved as both .png (for quick viewing) and .pkl (interactive Matplotlib figure). Reload a .pkl interactively with option [3] at the rerun prompt, or directly:

import pickle, matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig = pickle.load(open("plots/sea_state.pkl", "rb"))
plt.show()

docs.title: run_handle_data
docs.text: Processes raw CFD time series into a standardised format ready for validation and identification.

docs.title: first run
docs.text:
python -m script.run_handle_data --case <name>.json

Config files ´.json´ live in inputs/handle_case/. The filename stem becomes the output folder name under data/handled/.

docs.title: rerun options
docs.text:
When the output folder already exists, the script prompts:

[1] erase and redo all     — reprocess + replot from scratch
[2] stop, do nothing
[3] load saved figures     — reopen existing .pkl plots interactively
[4] remake figures only    — reuse processed CSVs, regenerate plots

Option [4] is useful when tuning plot parameters without reprocessing data.

docs.title: what it does
docs.text:
1. Reads each CFD case folder from data/cfd/
  2. Instantiates a DataHandle object per case
  3. Calls processData() — computes radiation force, hydrostatic force, linear excitation force (fe_lin), and absorbed power
  4. Optionally resamples to a target dt
  5. Saves processed data and wave parameters to data/handled/<name>/data/
  6. Generates and saves plots to data/handled/<name>/plots/

docs.title: Input JSON config
docs.text:
{
  "wave_type": "regular",
  "cut_time": [50, 0],
  "duration": null,
  "hydro_sphere_pkl": "r5",
  "dt": 0.05,
  "cases": [
    {
      "T": 8.0,
      "H": 2.0,
      "damping": 120000,
      "stiffness": -280000,
      "tag": "example",
      "plot": true
    }
  ],
  "plot_options": {
    "sea_state": true,
    "power": true,
    "dynamics": true,
    "hydro": false,
    "3d": false,
    "variable": ["fe_lin", "x"]
  }
}

docs.title: top-level fields
docs.text: Field Type Description wave_type "regular" | "irregular" Type of wave used in the CFD simulation cut_time [float, float] Seconds to discard from [start, end] of the raw signal. Use 0 to keep to the edge duration float | null Maximum duration (s) to retain after the start cut. null keeps all remaining data hydro_sphere_pkl string Stem of the BEM .pkl file in source/models/bem/. e.g. "r5" loads r5.pkl dt float | null Target resampling timestep (s). null keeps the original CFD timestep cases list List of CFD cases to process (see below) plot_options dict Controls which plots are generated (see below)

docs.title: case labels
docs.text:
Each CFD case is assigned a label derived from its parameters. The label is used as the CSV filename stem and as the series label in plots:

Hs{H}p{dec}_Te{T}p{dec}_d{damping}_k{stiffness}

Example: Hs2p0_Te8p0_d120000_k-280000

An optional "tag" field in the case config appends a suffix: Hs2p0_Te8p0_d120000_k-280000_example.

docs.title: plot_options fields
docs.text: Field Type Description sea_state bool Wave spectrum, elevation time series, and sea state grid power bool Absorbed power time series, power grid, and accumulated energy dynamics bool Displacement, velocity time series, and phase plot (x vs ẋ) hydro bool Hydrodynamic force breakdown: draft, linear forces, CFD forces, linear vs nonlinear comparisons 3d bool 3D scatter of displacement, velocity, and wave elevation variable list of strings | false One time-series plot per named column from _data.csv. e.g. ["fe_lin", "x"]

docs.title: run_identify
docs.text: Identifies model parameters or data-driven surrogates from CFD reference data using a pluggable scheme system.

docs.title: first run
docs.text:
python -m script.run_identify --case <name>.json

Config files <name>.json live in inputs/identify_case/. The filename stem becomes the output folder name under source/models/.

docs.title: rerun options
docs.text:
When the output folder already exists, the script prompts:

[1] erase and redo
[2] stop, do nothing
[3] load saved figures     — reopen existing .pkl plots interactively
[4] save with date suffix  — run and save under <name>_YYYYMMDD (keeps existing folder)

Option [4] is useful to keep previous identification results while running a new one.

docs.title: what it does
docs.text:
1. Loads the base model definition from source/models/<base_model>/model.json
  2. Creates a DDFeed — loads training data and runs scheme.prep()
  3. Creates an Optimizer — owns simulation helpers and delegates to scheme.run()
  4. Computes time margins (t_warmup, t_causal) from the base model and BEM data
  5. Saves identified parameters, result JSON, simulation CSVs and plots to source/models/<name>/identification/

docs.title: Scheme: viscous_drag
docs.text: Identifies the quadratic drag coefficient \(c_v\) in \(F_{visc} = -c_v |\dot{x}| \dot{x}\).

docs.title: input JSON config
docs.text:
{
  "scheme": "viscous_drag",
  "base_model": "linear",
  "waves_train": ["example_cases", "other_cases"],
  "scheme_params": {
    "type": ["force", "response"],
    "search": ["opt", "grid"],
    "base_force": "fhyd_lin",
    "c_v_min": 0,
    "c_v_max": 5000,
    "n_points": 50,
    "objective": "rmse_x"
  },
  "solver": {
    "method": "rk4",
    "dt": 0.05,
    "interpolation": {"fe": false, "fk": false, "eta_hs": false}
  }
}

docs.title: scheme_params fields
Per-case vs global identification
docs.text:
For every method, viscous_drag always produces two \(c_v\) values:

  • per-case — \(c_v\) fitted independently to each wave case (captures sea-state variability)
  • global — single \(c_v\) fitted across all cases pooled together → written to model.json

docs.title: JSON output
docs.text:
{
  "scheme": "viscous_drag",
  "objective": {"name": "rmse_x", "direction": "minimize"},
  "results": {
    "force_opt": {
      "c_v_global": 1850.0,
      "metric_global": 0.09,
      "metric_label": "rmse_x",
      "c_v_per_case": {"case_label_1": 1700.0, "case_label_2": 1950.0},
      "metric_per_case": {"case_label_1": 0.07, "case_label_2": 0.11},
      "c_v_mean": 1825.0,
      "c_v_std": 125.0
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Scheme: pi_gain
docs.text: Identifies per-sea-state PI controller gains \((B_{pto},\ K_{pto})\) that maximise an objective (default: mean absorbed power).

docs.title: input JSON config
docs.text:
{
  "scheme": "pi_gain",
  "base_model": "linear",
  "waves_train": [
    {"type": "cfd_case", "case_name": "example_cases"},
    {"type": "synthetic", "T": 7.0, "H": 2.0, "duration": 120.0}
  ],
  "scheme_params": {
    "method": ["analytical", "grid"],
    "B_min": 0,
    "B_max": 1000000,
    "K_min": -1000000,
    "K_max": 1000000,
    "n_B": 20,
    "n_K": 20,
    "objective": {"name": "mean_P_abs", "direction": "maximize"},
    "stability": {"enabled": true, "r": 5.0},
    "n_jobs": -1
  },
  "solver": {
    "method": "rk4",
    "dt": 0.05,
    "interpolation": {}
  }
}

docs.title: waves_train entry fields
docs.text:
Each dict in waves_train must have a "type" key:

"type": "cfd_case" — load from a handled CFD folder

"type": "synthetic" — generate a synthetic wave signal on the fly:

Wave supports the following fields:

Field Type Default Options / values Description type string — "synthetic" Source type selector wave_type (→ Wave.type) string "reg" "reg" (regular sinusoid) · "irr" (irregular JONSWAP) Wave type T float — any positive float (s) Wave period (regular) or peak period (irregular) H float — any positive float (m) Wave height (regular) or significant wave height (irregular) gamma float None any positive float JONSWAP peak enhancement factor — used only when wave_type = "irr" t_end (→ duration) float 100.0 any positive float (s) Signal duration dt float 0.01 any positive float (s) Time step — taken from solver.dt w_end float 8.0 any positive float (rad/s) Upper limit of frequency axis dw float 0.01 any positive float (rad/s) Frequency resolution

docs.title: scheme_params fields
JSON output
docs.text:
{
  "scheme": "pi_gain",
  "base_model": "linear",
  "objective": {"name": "mean_P_abs", "direction": "maximize"},
  "stability": {"enabled": true, "r": 5.0},
  "n_cases": 12,
  "results": {
    "grid": {
      "B_per_case": {"case_label": 42000.0},
      "K_per_case": {"case_label": -15000.0},
      "metric_per_case": {"case_label": 1250.3},
      "metric_label": "mean P_abs [W]"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Multiple entries
docs.text:
Field Accepts list? Effect waves_train yes (all schemes) entries pooled into one training dataset type + search yes (viscous_drag) cartesian product → one pass per combination method yes (pi_gain) one pass per value solver no single solver shared across all passes — run separate config files to compare solvers

All entries in waves_train are loaded and merged into a single flat pool of wave cases. Identification runs on all of them together — there is no separate pass per entry.

For viscous_drag, the global \(c_v\) is optimised over the concatenated signal from all cases at once, and each case also gets its own per-case \(c_v\). Adding more entries widens the training distribution.

For pi_gain, gains are always per sea state — each loaded wave case gets its own optimal \((B_{pto}, K_{pto})\). Adding more entries simply extends the set of sea states covered.

docs.title: Other keys
docs.text:
Field Type Options / values Description base_model string folder name under source/models/ — currently: "linear" · "none" disables physics Base physics model to augment with viscous drag waves_train list[string] stems of folders under data/handled/ Training cases. Multiple entries are pooled into one dataset scheme_params dict see table below Scheme-specific parameters solver dict see table below Forward simulation settings

solver:

Field Type Default Options / values Description method string "rk4" "euler" · "rk2" · "rk4" (case-insensitive) ODE integration scheme dt float — any positive float (s) Fixed timestep interpolation dict {} keys: "fe", "fk", "eta_hs" — values: true / false Per-force-term interpolation flags. Empty dict disables all ---

docs.title: Output structure
docs.text:
source/models/<name>/
├── <name>.json               ← copy of the config used
├── model.json                ← model definition updated with identified parameters
├── run.log
└── identification/
    ├── result.json           ← identified parameters and objective value per method
    ├── data/
    │   └── *.csv             ← simulated time series at best parameter values
    └── plots/
        ├── *.png
        └── *.pkl             ← interactive figure snapshots

docs.title: run_validate
docs.text: Simulates one or more models against CFD reference data and computes comparison metrics. Accepts lists for all major fields and runs every combination of models, wave sources, solvers, and simulation modes in a single execution.

docs.title: first run
docs.text:
python -m script.run_validate --case <name>.json

Config files <name>.json live in inputs/validate_case/. The filename stem becomes the output folder name under out/validated_case/.

docs.title: rerun options
docs.text:
When the output folder already exists, the script prompts:

[1] erase and redo
[2] stop, do nothing
[3] load saved figures     — reopen existing .pkl plots interactively
[4] save with date suffix  — run and save under <name>_YYYYMMDD (keeps existing folder)

docs.title: what it does
docs.text:
1. Loads each model definition from source/models/<name>/model.json
  2. Loads wave data from each wave_sources entry
  3. For every combination of (model × wave source × solver × eta input × simulation mode): runs a forward simulation
  4. Clips each simulated trajectory to the valid window (t_warmup, t_causal) computed from the model
  5. Computes comparison metrics against the CFD reference
  6. Saves result.json, simulation CSVs and plots to out/validated_case/<name>/

docs.title: Full example
docs.text:
{
  "models": [
    {"name": "linear"},
    {"name": "linear_viscous"}
  ],
  "wave_sources": [
    {"type": "cfd_case", "case_name": "example_cases"}
  ],
  "solvers": [
    {"method": "rk4", "dt": 0.05, "interpolation": {}},
    {"method": "rk2", "dt": 0.05, "interpolation": {"fe": false}}
  ],
  "eta_inputs": [
    {"type": "true"}
  ],
  "simulation": [
    {"type": "closed_loop"}
  ],
  "plot_options": {
    "states": true,
    "forces": false
  }
}

docs.title: Config fields
docs.text: Field Type Options / values Description models list[dict] name: folder under source/models/ Models to validate. Each entry must contain model.json wave_sources list[dict] type: "cfd_case" · case_name: stem under data/handled/ Wave data sources solvers list[dict] method: "euler" · "rk2" · "rk4" · dt: float (s) · interpolation: see below Solver configurations eta_inputs list[dict] type: "true" (measured CFD elevation \(\eta(t)\)) Wave elevation input simulation list[dict] type: "closed_loop" (PTO feedback included) Simulation mode plot_options dict states: bool · forces: bool Controls which plots are generated

docs.title: solvers.interpolation
docs.text:
Per-force-term flags — true re-evaluates at each RK sub-stage, false freezes to step-start (ZOH):

Key Force term "fe" Linear excitation force \(f_e^{lin}\) "fk" Nonlinear Froude–Krylov force "eta_hs" Wave elevation for nonlinear hydrostatic

Empty dict {} enables all terms (recommended for rk4 / rk2).

docs.title: plot_options fields
docs.text: Field Type Default Options / values Description states bool true true / false Time series of \(x\), \(\dot{x}\), \(\eta\), \(f_{pto}\), \(P_{abs}\) forces bool false true / false Time series of individual force terms

docs.title: Multiple entries
docs.text:
Field Accepts list? Effect models yes one simulation pass per model wave_sources yes each source run against all models and solvers solvers yes each solver configuration run against all combinations eta_inputs yes each input type run against all combinations simulation yes each simulation mode run against all combinations

All combinations are run in a single execution. result.json stores metrics keyed by model name and case label, covering every combination.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Metrics are computed for each simulated trajectory against the CFD reference:

Name Description "rmse_x" RMSE of displacement \(x\) [m] "rmse_xdot" RMSE of velocity \(\dot{x}\) [m/s] "nrmse_x" Normalised RMSE of \(x\) "nrmse_xdot" Normalised RMSE of \(\dot{x}\) "mean_P_abs" Mean absorbed power \(P_{abs}\) [W] "rmse_P_abs" RMSE of absorbed power [W]

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
out/validated_case/<name>/
├── <name>.json               ← copy of the config used
├── run.log
├── result.json               ← metric summary for all models and sea states
├── data/
│   └── <label>_simrun.csv    ← simulated time series per case per model
└── plots/
    ├── scatter_<metric>.png / .pkl
    └── timeseries_<label>.png / .pkl

docs.title: Model types
docs.text:
A model in HIVE is a folder under models/ containing a model.json file. The JSON records the model's physics components, identified parameters, and metadata. Currently supported model types:

Model key Description linear Cummins equation with radiation state-space, linear PTO linear_viscous As linear, plus quadratic drag $c_v

Models identified by run_identify inherit a base model's model.json and add or update the identified parameters.

docs.title: model.json structure
docs.text:
{
  "type": "linear_viscous",
  "hydro_sphere_pkl": "r5",
  "radiation": {
    "A": [[...], ...],
    "B": [[...]],
    "C": [[...]],
    "D": [[...]]
  },
  "hydrostatic": {
    "K_hs": 142000.0
  },
  "added_mass_inf": 450.0,
  "mass": 1200.0,
  "c_v": 1850.0,
  "t_warmup": 15.0,
  "t_causal": 3.2
}

The radiation block holds the state-space matrices \((A_{rad}, B_{rad}, C_{rad}, D_{rad})\) fitted from the BEM IRF. These are written by run_handle_data during the first call that initialises the BEM data.

docs.title: SimRun
docs.text:
SimRun is the class responsible for running a single forward simulation. It:

  1. Loads the model definition from model.json
  2. Instantiates the radiation state integrator
  3. Steps the ODE forward using the chosen solver
  4. Returns a dataset attribute (a pandas.DataFrame) with the same column schema as DataHandle

Because SimRun and DataHandle expose the same .dataset and .label interface, they can be mixed in plotter calls.

docs.title: ODE solvers
docs.text:
The solver block in validate and identify configs selects the numerical integrator:

"solver": {
  "method": "RK4",
  "dt": 0.05,
  "interpolation": {}
}
Method Description RK4 4th-order Runge–Kutta (recommended) RK2 2nd-order Runge–Kutta (Heun's method) euler Forward Euler (1st order, fast but inaccurate)

The integration timestep dt is independent of the CFD data's native timestep. HIVE interpolates the forcing signals (wave elevation, excitation force) onto the solver grid using the scheme specified in interpolation.

docs.title: Warmup period
docs.text:
The radiation state-space system starts at rest (\(\mathbf{z}_{rad} = 0\)). It takes several wave periods for the radiation states to converge to their quasi-steady values. HIVE computes t_warmup automatically from the pole magnitudes of \(A_{rad}\):

\[ t_{warmup} = \frac{-\log(\epsilon)}{\min_k |\text{Re}(p_k)|} \]

where \(\epsilon\) is a small tolerance (default \(10^{-3}\)) and \(p_k\) are the eigenvalues of \(A_{rad}\). The value is logged in run.log and saved in result.json.

Metrics are computed only over \([t_{warmup},\; T_{end} - t_{causal}]\).

docs.title: Why interpolation is needed
docs.text:
The excitation force \(f_e^{lin}\) and wave elevation \(\eta\) are precomputed on a fixed grid — the timestep of the handled CFD data (set by dt in the handle config). The ODE solver may use a different timestep. At each stage of the integrator (e.g. the four stages of RK4), the forcing signals must be evaluated at intermediate time points that generally do not fall on the original grid, requiring interpolation.

Note that \(f_e^{lin}\) is state-independent — it does not depend on \(x\) or \(\dot{x}\) — so it is fully precomputed before integration begins. This is unlike the radiation force \(f_{rad}\), which is stepped forward as a state-space system at each stage, or \(f_{hs}\) and \(f_{pto}\), which are evaluated from the current state.

docs.title: Interpolation schemes
docs.text:
The interpolation dict in the solver config is passed directly to scipy.interpolate.interp1d via the kind keyword:

kind Description Accuracy "linear" (default) Piecewise linear between grid points 2nd order in grid spacing "nearest" Zero-order hold — value at nearest grid point 1st order (step function) "quadratic" Piecewise quadratic spline 3rd order "cubic" Piecewise cubic spline 4th order

docs.title: Consistency with the ODE solver
docs.text:
A subtle point: if you use RK4 ("method": "RK4") but hold the forcing constant within a step ("kind": "nearest"), the integration is effectively first-order in the forcing term. The radiation and restoring forces benefit from the full RK4 accuracy, but the excitation forcing does not. For best results, match the interpolation order to the solver:

  • RK4 / RK2: use "linear" or "cubic"
  • Euler: "nearest" (ZOH) is sufficient and cheapest

In practice, "linear" is a good default — it is cheap and ensures that \(f_e^{lin}\) varies smoothly across RK stages.

docs.title: Practical note on grid resolution
docs.text: The interpolation error decreases as the handled data timestep decreases. If you notice artefacts in simulated time series (especially at high frequencies), try reducing dt in the handle config to produce a finer forcing grid, rather than switching to a higher-order interpolation scheme.
